title: Module Resolution and ESM/CommonJS
summary: Understand how TypeScript finds imported files and how JavaScript modules run.
nestedConcepts: Resolve imports the way the runtime does

subtopics.title: Choose the module output model
subtopics.explanation: The `module` option controls how TypeScript interprets and emits JavaScript modules, including `import` and `export`. A browser bundler project and a Node.js ESM package can need different settings. Match the compiler configuration to the runtime or bundler that actually consumes the files.

subtopics.title: Resolve imports the way the runtime does
subtopics.explanation: `moduleResolution` decides how TypeScript follows an import to a file or package entry. The `bundler` mode models modern bundlers; `node16` and `nodenext` model Node’s ESM and CommonJS rules. A mismatch can make the editor accept an import that fails after deployment.

subtopics.title: Read package module metadata
subtopics.explanation: Package fields such as `type`, `exports`, and conditional exports affect which module file a runtime or bundler loads. A package may publish separate ESM and CommonJS entry points. Check the package metadata when an import works in one environment but fails in another.

subtopics.title: Handle ESM and CommonJS interop
subtopics.explanation: ES modules and CommonJS expose exports differently, so a default import can behave differently across packages and runtimes. TypeScript interop options adjust type checking or emitted helper code; they do not rewrite a package’s actual format. Verify the import with the production bundler or Node version.

subtopics.title: Verify the real import path
subtopics.explanation: When module resolution is unclear, build and run a small import through the same tool used in production. Check both the emitted JavaScript and the resolved package entry. Editor autocomplete alone is not proof that the deployed runtime can load the module.

foundations.overview: Module resolution is the process of finding the file behind an import. ESM uses import and export syntax. CommonJS uses require and module.exports. Package settings and build tools affect how these formats connect, so a type-checking success does not always guarantee runtime loading.
foundations.mentalModel: A map can point to a room that is locked; finding a file is not the same as loading it.
foundations.whyItMatters: Many production bugs come from a mismatch between what TypeScript resolves and what Node or a bundler runs.

keyTakeaways: module chooses the output module format.
moduleResolution controls how imports are located.
package.json type and exports influence runtime behavior.
Interop options affect default import compatibility.
Verify the actual runtime or bundler path.
